premise: A political drama about the last days of Herbert Chitepo and how his assassination affected the trajectory of post-independence Zimbabwe.
title: CHITEPO · 1975
overview: The research reveals the covert political landscape of Lusaka in 1975 during the Southern African liberation struggle. Exiled ZANU leaders operated under heavy surveillance from Zambian authorities and Rhodesian intelligence agents. Herbert Chitepo led the nationalist movement until a vehicle bomb killed him outside his home. This film focuses on the final days before the assassination and the immediate fracture of the liberation leadership. The story traces how the resulting arrests altered the path to Zimbabwean independence.

boxes.summary: Forensic records track Herbert Chitepo's Volkswagen Beetle before and after the explosion. Police blueprints establish the exact location where the explosive device was mounted inside the wheel arch. Investigators examined the vehicle frame to calculate the force of the detonation. The physical remains of the car provided key evidence for post-assassination inquiries.
boxes.description: Archival blueprints and police forensic reports document the precise make, model, modification history, and bomb placement within Herbert Chitepo's Volkswagen Beetle.
boxes.rationale: The staging of the fatal March 1975 explosion requires technical accuracy for visual effects and physical prop reconstruction.
boxes.name: CHITEPO VEHICLE MECHANICS

boxes.summary: Municipal records detail the layout of Herbert Chitepo's home in Chilenje South. Chilenje was an established residential township in Lusaka. The property featured basic perimeter security and fencing common to middle-class suburban lots. Photographic surveys document the access roads and neighboring structures surrounding the compound.
boxes.description: Photographs, municipal plans, and surveys record the layout and security fencing of the Chitepo residence in Lusaka's Chilenje South neighborhood.
boxes.rationale: Location scouts and set decorators must match the physical perimeter where the assassination was planned and executed.
boxes.name: LUSAKA SUBURBAN ARCHITECTURE

boxes.summary: Meeting records show serious friction within the ZANU Dare reChimurenga leadership council in early 1975. Diplomatic transcripts document growing splits between civilian political leaders and front-line military commanders. Herbert Chitepo managed these factions while directing the external guerrilla campaign. The depositions record deep ideological disputes immediately preceding his death.
boxes.description: Meeting minutes, transcripts, and witness depositions detail the internal debates between DARE council members and military commanders in early 1975.
boxes.rationale: The script requires authentic ideological arguments, factional vocabulary, and interpersonal tensions among the nationalist elite.
boxes.name: ZANU LEADERSHIP DYNAMICS

boxes.summary: Zambian police logs detail the mass arrests of ZANU cadres following the March 1975 explosion. The Preservation of Public Security Act gave Zambian authorities legal power to hold suspects without trial. Special Branch officers conducted interrogations across Lusaka police stations. Detainees were held under emergency powers while commissions reviewed the case.
boxes.description: Zambian police logs, prison records, and Special Branch reports establish the detention procedures and interrogation methods used during the post-assassination crackdown.
boxes.rationale: Depicting the mass arrests of ZANU cadres requires accurate procedural uniforms, holding facilities, and institutional behavior.
boxes.name: ZAMBIAN SECURITY POLICING

boxes.summary: Declassified operational files outline covert cross-border intelligence work run by Rhodesian services out of Salisbury. Branch Six of the Central Intelligence Organisation managed surveillance networks across Zambia. Field handlers collected data on nationalist leadership movements in Lusaka. These records show how state agencies targeted exile commands outside Rhodesian borders.
boxes.description: Declassified Central Intelligence Organisation operational files and handler field notes detail the cross-border covert operations run out of Salisbury.
boxes.rationale: Writers need concrete timelines and operational terminology for intelligence officers manipulating nationalist divisions.
boxes.name: RHODESIAN INTELLIGENCE OPERATIONS

boxes.summary: Photographs from the mid-1970s illustrate the diverse attire worn by liberation leaders in Lusaka. Exiled figures wore tailored Western suits for formal diplomatic meetings. Field commanders wore military fatigues during operational briefings. Traditional African textiles appeared alongside everyday civilian clothing across public gatherings.
boxes.description: Photographic records from the mid-1970s illustrate the tailored Western suits, military fatigues, and traditional fabrics worn by liberation leaders in Lusaka.
boxes.rationale: Costume design must reflect social status, diplomatic posturing, and ideological alignment through clothing choices.
boxes.name: EXILE DIPLOMATIC ATTIRE

boxes.summary: Archival photographic surveys document the standard transport fleet active in 1975 Lusaka. Streets carried government-issued Land Rovers alongside private sedans and bush taxis. Traffic centered heavily around major hubs like the Kafue Roundabout in the central business district. Nationalist organizations depended on these shared vehicles to move personnel between offices and suburban safehouses.
boxes.description: Photographic surveys and vehicle registries identify the specific makes of private sedans, government Land Rovers, and bush taxis common to 1975 Lusaka.
boxes.rationale: Exterior street scenes depend on period-accurate vehicle models to establish historical credibility.
boxes.name: URBAN TRANSPORT FLEETS

boxes.summary: Liberation movement headquarters in Lusaka relied on shortwave radio sets and fixed dial telephone systems. Exiled leaders sent cables and telegrams to maintain contact with foreign governments. International calls to Zambia required standard national routing prefixes and landlines. Office photographs show manual telex machines handling official outgoing statements.
boxes.description: Technical manuals and office photographs show the shortwave radio setups, dial telephones, and cablegram equipment available to exiled liberation movements.
boxes.rationale: Prop masters must source operational period hardware that dictated the speed of communication during the crisis.
boxes.name: MID-SEVENTIES TELECOMMUNICATIONS

boxes.summary: Oral histories describe conditions inside ZANU military training bases across Zambia and Tanzania. Cadres slept in basic barracks and conducted daily morning drills. Bases such as Takawira Base 1 managed strict ration distribution under severe supply constraints. Recruits shared communal living spaces and relied on scarce medical kits.
boxes.description: Oral histories and photographic collections from camps in Zambia and Tanzania describe rations, daily drills, sleeping quarters, and medical supplies.
boxes.rationale: Visual and narrative departments must construct the physical hardships faced by rank-and-file guerrilla fighters.
boxes.name: LIBERATION CAMP LIFE

boxes.summary: Audio field recordings from the 1970s show distinct regional dialects across the exile community. Leaders and fighters spoke various dialects of Shona, including Karanga, alongside Ndebele. Exiled figures frequently switched into Zambian English during administrative work. Settler authorities spoke in characteristic Rhodesian English accents.
boxes.description: Field audio recordings from the 1970s preserve regional Shona, Ndebele, Zambian English, and Rhodesian accents across social classes.
boxes.rationale: Voice coaches and actors need precise phonological references to ground regional and educational divides.
boxes.name: SOUTHERN AFRICAN DIALECTS

boxes.summary: Archival audio captures the sound environment of Lusaka throughout the 1970s. The city soundscape featured a mix of urban traffic, commercial market noise, and industrial machinery. Local radio stations and public venues broadcast contemporary Zamrock recordings. Residential areas like Chilenje retained quieter backgrounds dominated by ambient birdsong and passing road traffic.
boxes.description: Audio archives and historical ambient recordings capture the balance of traffic, market crowds, industrial hum, and birdsong in 1970s Lusaka.
boxes.rationale: Sound designers must build a naturalistic acoustic environment specific to a growing post-colonial capital city.
boxes.name: LUSAKA SOUNDSCAPES

boxes.summary: Newspapers from March 1975 show the media reaction to Herbert Chitepo's death. The Times of Zambia carried front-page coverage of the blast and the subsequent state security actions. The Rhodesia Herald reported the incident from the perspective of the Salisbury government. State radio bulletins in Lusaka broadcast emergency public announcements.
boxes.description: Archival copies of the Times of Zambia, Rhodesia Herald, and Radio Zambia broadcasts capture the media coverage surrounding the assassination.
boxes.rationale: Set decorators and screenwriters need the exact headlines, graphic layouts, and broadcast rhetoric of breaking news reports.
boxes.name: PRINT AND BROADCAST MEDIA

boxes.summary: Visual archives preserve the physical appearances and mannerisms of the primary political figures. Kenneth Kaunda was recognized for his formal public address style and signature personal accessories. Josiah Tongogara possessed a commanding military bearing captured in period portraits. Herbert Chitepo maintained the composed, intellectual demeanor of an experienced jurist.
boxes.description: Archival footage and portrait photography establish the physical statures, facial features, and mannerisms of Herbert Chitepo, Kenneth Kaunda, and Josiah Tongogara.
boxes.rationale: The casting department requires visual benchmarks to select actors who convincingly embody key historical figures.
boxes.name: POLITICAL FIGURES CASTING

boxes.summary: Financial ledgers record the operational spending of exiled liberation movements in Lusaka. Nationalists handled transactions using Zambian kwacha, British sterling, and international travel stipends. Funds flowed through external solidarity committees to support office operations. Leaders relied on documented cash allowances to secure transport and maintain properties.
boxes.description: Bank ledgers and liberation support committee records detail the flow of Zambian kwacha, British sterling, and cash stipends to exiled leaders.
boxes.rationale: The script must accurately represent the logistics of movement funding and the physical currency passed between operators.
boxes.name: CURRENCY AND FINANCIAL LOGISTICS

boxes.summary: Nationalist leaders met informally across designated social spaces in Lusaka. Activists gathered in neighborhoods such as the Ridgeway district and regional hotel lounges. Exiled cadres utilized suburban residences for sensitive political negotiations. These social hubs offered spaces to debate policy away from formal offices.
boxes.description: Memoirs, interviews, and urban maps document the specific bars, hotel lobbies, and private homes where Lusaka-based nationalists held informal meetings.
boxes.rationale: Location scouts need to identify interiors matching the relaxed social hubs where crucial alliances formed.
boxes.name: EXILE SOCIAL SPACES

boxes.summary: Legal records and political histories trace the succession battle that followed Chitepo's assassination. The removal of the external chairman disrupted the existing ZANU hierarchy. The resulting leadership vacuum opened the path for Robert Mugabe to consolidate power by 1980. The event set lasting precedents for governance in post-independence Zimbabwe.
boxes.description: Legal transcripts, commission findings, and policy speeches trace the long-term political impact of Chitepo's death on the 1980 Zimbabwean power structure.
boxes.rationale: The screenplay framing requires historical clarity on how the 1975 power vacuum enabled Robert Mugabe's rise to ZANU leadership.
boxes.name: POST-INDEPENDENCE SUCCESSION PRECEDENTS

boxes.summary: The Special International Commission on the Assassination of Herbert Wiltshire Chitepo produced transcripts across 1975 and 1976. Representatives from multiple African nations heard sworn witness testimony. Court records preserved depositions from imprisoned ZANU officials. The commission compiled official evidentiary submissions to determine institutional responsibility for the bombing.
boxes.description: Official hearing transcripts, multinational committee proceedings, and evidentiary submissions generated by the Special International Commission on the Assassination of Herbert Wiltshire Chitepo in 1975–1976.
boxes.rationale: It serves as the primary investigative and legal spine connecting Zambian state policing, ZANU leadership factionalism, diplomatic tensions, and the contested narrative shaping post-independence Zimbabwean succession.
boxes.name: CHITEPO COMMISSION OF INQUIRY

boxes.summary: Diplomatic cables document the 1974 to 1975 Southern African détente initiative. Zambia, Tanzania, and Frontline States negotiated directly with South African representatives. Kenneth Kaunda engaged in talks regarding political transitions in Rhodesia. These regional summits increased pressure on exile groups to pause military offensives.
boxes.description: Diplomatic cables, summit memoranda, and bilateral communiqués between Zambia, South Africa, Tanzania, and Frontline States during the 1974–1975 Southern African détente initiative.
boxes.rationale: The geopolitical pressure of détente directly influenced Kaunda's policing, internal ZANU leadership friction, Rhodesian intelligence moves, and the subsequent commission of inquiry.
boxes.name: DETENTE REGIONAL DIPLOMACY

boxes.summary: Explosive ordnance reports analyze the mechanism that destroyed the Volkswagen Beetle. Forensic specialists identified the weapon as a military-grade TNT charge positioned under the chassis. Blast overpressure tests show how the upward explosion sheared through the floorboards. Post-blast assessments documented shrapnel dispersion patterns across the driveway.
boxes.description: Technical analysis, post-blast investigation records, and photographic evidence detailing the TNT landmine mechanism, blast physics, and shrapnel dispersion patterns from the assassination.
boxes.rationale: It bridges vehicle mechanics, Rhodesian intelligence sabotage methods, the Zambian police crackdown, and the international commission of inquiry's physical evidence.
boxes.name: EXPLOSIVE ORDNANCE FORENSICS

boxes.summary: Archival accounts document the late 1974 Nhari rebellion within ZANLA guerrilla ranks. Front-line cadres led by Thomas Nhari protested against the Dare reChimurenga over poor supplies. Military commanders suppressed the mutiny with armed force. The leadership carried out subsequent trials, purges, and executions that destabilized ZANU before Chitepo was killed.
boxes.description: Historical documentation, trial notes, and survivor testimonies detailing the late 1974 internal ZANLA mutiny led by Thomas Nhari and the subsequent purges and executions sanctioned by ZANU leadership.
boxes.rationale: The mutiny and its violent aftermath directly catalyzed the factional paranoia, detentions, and security crises leading up to Chitepo's assassination and the subsequent Commission of Inquiry.
boxes.name: NHARI REBELLION FALLOUT

boxes.summary: Zambian prison records identify the detention facilities used during the crackdown on ZANU cadres. Hundreds of officials were incarcerated at Kabwe and the Mpima Remand facility. Detainees were also transferred to isolated camps like Mboroma. Architectural floor plans document cell sizes, perimeter walls, and security protocols in these state institutions.
boxes.description: Architectural blueprints, site photographs, and prisoner records documenting the specific Zambian prisons and holding camps, such as Mpima Remand and Mboroma, where ZANU cadres were detained after Chitepo's death.
boxes.rationale: Following the assassination, hundreds of ZANU and ZANLA leaders and fighters were mass-arrested across Lusaka, directly intersecting with political leadership dynamics, Zambian police procedures, the post-Nhari purges, and production location choices.
boxes.name: FRONTLINE STATES DETENTION SITES

boxes.summary: Photographs document Herbert Chitepo's state funeral proceedings in Lusaka in March 1975. Zambian officials organized formal protocol rites for the initial burial in Zambia. Diplomatic delegations attended the public services under police escort. His remains were later repatriated to Zimbabwe in 1981 for reburial at the National Heroes Acre in Harare.
boxes.description: Photographic archives, diplomatic protocols, and eyewitness accounts documenting Herbert Chitepo's state-facilitated funeral in Lusaka and subsequent repatriation rites.
boxes.rationale: Chitepo's funeral was a pivotal public event intersecting Zambian state security, diplomatic attendance, liberation movement tensions, media coverage, and traditional mourning practices.
boxes.name: FUNERAL AND MEMORIAL RITUALS

## Chilenje House 394

Chilenje House 394  was a house in Chilenje, Lusaka, Zambia in which the then President, Dr. Kenneth Kaunda lived from January 1960 to December 1962. It is from this house he directed the fight for independence of Northern Rhodesia (now the Republic of Zambia) which was achieved on 24th October,1964.

The site was declared a National Monument on 23rd October,1968, and has since been managed by the National Heritage Conservation Commission.

The house is two bed-roomed, with a kitchen and living room. Three houses reside on the protected monument and they have all been restored to their 1962 conditions as much as nearly possible.

House No. 394 has been redecorated in its original colour scheme, and much of the furniture and personal effects used by the Kenneth Kaunda family at that time has been replaced in the original positions. House No. 395 contains displays illustrating the history and growth of Lusaka from the earliest times and the political development of Zambia. House No. 393 is the caretaker’s residence.

Nelson Mandela’s “Madiba” shirts were dramatically different  from the conventional western suits worn by most politicians in South Africa and around the world. They were also the opposite of the hateful, drab prison garb that he was forced to wear for almost three decades.
He opted to wear these shirts because he did not want to be confined by a suit and tie. Africa’s climate is very hot and he wanted something that was elegant and easy to wear, that would reflect the bright colors of Africa and his easy, laid back leadership style.”

This modest documentary revisits the brief, almost-forgotten history of “Zamrock” – or at least what remains of it, which appears to be very little beyond the back catalogue of its leading band, Witch. Witch’s rhythmic blend of British blues, funk, psychedelic and garage rock has aged very well, and reissues of their albums in the 2010s found a new audience, including Italian film-maker Gio Arlotta, who consequently undertook an expedition to Zambia to try to find the band, accompanied by two young Dutch musicians, Jacco Gardner and Nic Mauskovic

evidence.text: The death and rebirth of the distinctive sounds of Zambia · Global Voices. One of the unique sounds that emerged and gained popularity during this time — the 1970s — is “Zamrock.” It combined psychedelic rock, funk, and traditional Zambian music, and represented a desire to break away from colonial influences while still incorporating Western musical styles. Bands like WITCH (a backronym for “We Intend To Cause Havoc”) played with imported Western styles but added their own indigenous twist, acknowledging their African identity in their music. Other noteworthy artists who were known for this music genre include The Peace , Amanaz , Chrissy “Zebby” Tembo, and Paul Ngozi and his Ngozi Family. Ngozi was a legendary Zambian musician in the 1970s and 1980s

## About State House

## Chilenje House 394

Chilenje House 394  was a house in Chilenje, Lusaka, Zambia in which the then President, Dr. Kenneth Kaunda lived from January 1960 to December 1962. It is from this house he directed the fight for independence of Northern Rhodesia (now the Republic of Zambia) which was achieved on 24th October,1964.

The site was declared a National Monument on 23rd October,1968, and has since been managed by the National Heritage Conservation Commission.

The house is two bed-roomed, with a kitchen and living room. Three houses reside on the protected monument and they have all been restored to their 1962 conditions as much as nearly possible.

House No. 394 has been redecorated in its original colour scheme, and much of the furniture and personal effects used by the Kenneth Kaunda family at that time has been replaced in the original positions. House No. 395 contains displays illustrating the history and growth of Lusaka from the earliest times and the political development of Zambia. House No. 393 is the caretaker’s residence.

Kenneth David Kaunda , (April 28, 1924 - June 17, 2021) served as the first president of Zambia , from 1964 to 1991. He played a major role in Zambia's independence movement which sought to free itself from Rhodesia and white minority rule. For his efforts, Kaunda suffered imprisonment and several confrontations with rival groups.
Kenneth Kaunda died on June 17, 2021 at Mina Soko Medical Centre in Lusaka. The government announced a 21-day mourning period.
The rest of Zambia is very sparsely populated, particularly the west and the northeast; the majority of people make their living as subsistence farmers.
Kenneth Kaunda was the first President of Zambia and one of the major leaders of Zambia's independence movement.

The collapse of apartheid and the advent of democracy in South Africa was regionally supported by a group of southern African states called the Frontline States. These were Angola, Botswana, Lesotho, Mozambique, Swaziland, Tanzania, Zambia and, from 1980, Zimbabwe. The Frontline States were formed in 1970 to co-ordinate their responses to apartheid and formulate a uniform policy towards apartheid government and the liberation movement. For the liberation movement in South Africa, the formation of the Frontline States was a welcomed development and a new front in the fight against apartheid. However, these states still found it difficult to pursue their goals of ending apartheid. # Nhari rebellion explained

The **Nhari Rebellion** occurred in November 1974, amidst the Rhodesian Bush War , when members of the Zimbabwe African National Liberation Army (ZANLA) in Chifombo, Zambia (near the border with Mozambique) rebelled against the leadership of the political party it was attached to, the Zimbabwe African National Union (ZANU).

The uprising was led by Thomas Nhari (from whom it takes its name), [[1]]() and supported by Noel Mukono and Simpson Mutambanengwe . [[2]]() Nhari and his followers were motivated by the belief that the members of the ZANU High Command, based in Lusaka , were leading an overly extravagant lifestyle, contrary to the party's Maoist principles. Ken Flower , the head of the Rhodesian Central Intelligence Organisation , sponsored the rebellion, which was carried out by "willing conspirators". [[3]]() [[4]]()

## Aftermath

The rebellion ultimately proved to be unsuccessful, with the rebellious guerrillas being forcibly put down by ZANU defence chief Josiah Tongogara . [[5]]()

prior_art.premise: A political drama about the last days of Herbert Chitepo and how his assassination affected the trajectory of post-independence Zimbabwe.

unclaimed_angles.prompt: Center the story on a Zambian civil servant living next door to Chitepo who monitors the factional shifts with rising dread.
unclaimed_angles.angle: The narrative is framed entirely through the eyes of an ordinary Lusaka neighbor who observes the escalating factional paranoia surrounding the Chitepo compound.
unclaimed_angles.why: None of the political films adopt an external civilian bystander who remains detached from party logistics.

unclaimed_angles.prompt: Follow a Zambian Special Branch inspector trying to map out Rhodesian infiltration inside the liberation movement before the bomb detonates.
unclaimed_angles.angle: The film functions as an institutional procedural tracking the Zambian police team that attempted to prevent the car bomb explosion.
unclaimed_angles.why: None of the historical titles focus on a host-nation law enforcement bureaucracy caught between diplomatic neutrality and counter-assassination failure.

unclaimed_angles.prompt: End the film with the international commission drafting a deliberately ambiguous verdict to preserve the regional front against Rhodesia.
unclaimed_angles.angle: The drama concludes with an administrative commission that quietly covers up the true perpetrators to protect fragile frontline state alliances.
unclaimed_angles.why: None of the existing political assassination stories terminate in a bureaucratic diplomatic compromise.

neighbors.overview: The true story of the rise to power and brutal assassination of the formerly vilified and later redeemed leader of the independent Congo, Patrice Lumumba. Using newly discovered historical evidence, Haitian-born and later Congo-raised writer and director Raoul Peck renders an emotional and tautly woven account of the mail clerk and beer salesman with a flair for oratory and an uncompromising belief in the capacity of his homeland to build a prosperous nation independent of its former Belgian overlords. Lumumba emerges here as the heroic sacrificial lamb dubiously portrayed by the international media and led to slaughter by commercial and political interests in Belgium, the United States, the international community, and Lumumba's own administration; a true story of political intrigue and murder where political entities, captains of commerce, and the military dovetail in their quest for economic and political hegemony.
neighbors.title: Lumumba

neighbors.overview: Documentary about African political leader Patrice Lumumba, who was Prime Minister of Zaire (now Democratic Republic of Congo) when he was assassinated in 1961.
neighbors.title: Lumumba: Death of a Prophet

neighbors.overview: Paratrooper commander Colonel Mathieu, a former French Resistance fighter during World War II, is sent to Algeria to reinforce efforts to squelch the uprisings of the Algerian War. There he faces Ali la Pointe, a former petty criminal who, as the leader of the Algerian Front de Liberation Nationale, directs terror strategies against the colonial French government occupation. As each side resorts to ever-increasing brutality, no violent act is too unthinkable.
neighbors.title: The Battle of Algiers

neighbors.overview: Gunman Flame and his partner Citron assassinate Nazi collaborators for the Danish resistance. Assigned targets by their Allies-connected leader, Aksel Winther, they relish the opportunity to begin targeting the Nazis themselves. When they begin to doubt the validity of their assignments, their morally complicated task becomes even more labyrinthine.
neighbors.title: Flame & Citron

neighbors.overview: Bill O'Neal infiltrates the Black Panthers on the orders of FBI Agent Mitchell and J. Edgar Hoover. As Black Panther Chairman Fred Hampton ascends—falling for a fellow revolutionary en route—a battle wages for O’Neal’s soul.
neighbors.title: Judas and the Black Messiah

neighbors.overview: To commemorate the fiftieth anniversary of THE BATTLE OF ALGIERS, we revisited our edit of the film and interviews with director Gillo Pontecorvo and producer Saadi Yacef, who discuss the process of representing Algeria's struggle for independence and the challenges of presenting a balanced view of the conflict.
neighbors.title: Marxist Poetry: The Making of The Battle of Algiers

neighbors.overview: Jazz and decolonization are intertwined in a powerful narrative that recounts one of the tensest episodes of the Cold War.
neighbors.title: Soundtrack to a Coup d'Etat

neighbors.overview: A tribute to the controversial black activist and leader of the struggle for black liberation. He hit bottom during his imprisonment in the '50s, he became a Black Muslim and then a leader in the Nation of Islam. His assassination in 1965 left a legacy of self-determination and racial pride.
neighbors.title: Malcolm X

neighbors.overview: A trading company manager travels up an African river to find a missing outpost head and discovers the depth of evil in humanity's soul.
neighbors.title: Heart of Darkness

neighbors.overview: After witnessing his billionaire boss' murder and being framed for the crime, Cole Reed boards a cargo ship on a one-man crusade to avenge his boss' death only to discover an international conspiracy.
neighbors.title: Mutiny

neighbors.overview: Edward Wilson, the only witness to his father's suicide and member of the Skull and Bones Society while a student at Yale, is a morally upright young man who values honor and discretion, qualities that help him to be recruited for a career in the newly founded OSS. His dedication to his work does not come without a price though, leading him to sacrifice his ideals and eventually his family.
neighbors.title: The Good Shepherd
